messages:
ana: Quick sync — planning a "Commercial Composer" tier for Q2. Proposal: priority-lane add-on (latency SLO + routing priority), throughput-pack (reserved capacity with burst credits), and explicit per-route limits. Need to align on launch criteria, contractual language, and engineering scope. Can anyone join a 30m sync today?

liz: I can join at 3pm. Need clarity on target latency SLOs for priority lane (p50/p95) and what 'priority' actually buys customers.

sam: From product POV: target p95 <= 120ms for short prompts under priority lane, and a documented fallback path to standard tier. We should also spell out failure modes (queueing, eviction).

mohit: Engineering note — priority routing implies per-tenant queue isolation or token-limited windows. We can prototype with a soft-priority weight in the router, but strict isolation needs dedicated pools (adds cost). Rough estimate: +20% infra for first pilot.

ralph: We should quantify cost to the customer vs us. If reserved throughput-pack reduces per-token costs, legal/commercial will want clear uplift tables (e.g., reserved 10k reqs/day -> X discount).

legal: Heads-up: avoid 'unlimited' or 'guaranteed' without explicit SLOs and credits. Need fallback SLA text and termination/escape clauses for abuse. I'll draft standard clause options.

ana: @ana (typo) — ops-bot: can you surface last quarter's highest-consumed routes + burst patterns so we can size the throughput-pack?

ops-bot: Sure — pulling top routes and 99th percentile bursts. CSV exported here: https://internal.redwood/exports/top-routes-q4.csv :file_folder:

sam: Thanks. Two launch-criteria proposals from product: 1) Tech: successful pilot with 3 customers across 2 different workload classes for 4 weeks with no regression in baseline SLOs. 2) Biz: Pricing table finalized + legal language approved. 3) Ops: automated rollback & routing fallback tested. Thoughts?

liz: add quality guardrail: no >5% generation-quality regressions on evaluation suite for composer prompts. Otherwise we risk customer complaints if quantized models used.

mohit: Agree. Also call out instrumentation: token-level billing trace, per-tenant latency heatmaps, and per-route throttle metrics must be in the console before GA.

ralph: For packaging, suggest 3 SKUs: Composer Lite (soft-priority, small reserved band), Composer (priority lane + medium reserved), Composer Pro (dedicated pools + enterprise SLAs). We can map discounts to commit levels.

legal: I’ll prepare two contract templates: Pilot Addendum and Enterprise SLA. Pilot Addendum will include limited liability, pilot end date, & escape hatch. Enterprise SLA will include credits and termination triggers.

ana: Action items: 
- ana: book 30m sync 3pm today (will include eng, product, sales rep)
- liz: propose evaluation prompt set by EOD (quality guardrails)
- sam: draft pricing uplift tables + mapping to commit tiers (by tomorrow)
- mohit: quick infra cost estimate and a list of engineering blockers (24h)
- legal: draft pilot addendum template (48h)
- ops-bot: attach burst CSV and perf traces to the thread

sam: One more: we need a clear customer-facing wording for 'priority' — recommend "routing priority with documented SLO and fallback". Keeps expectations set.

liz: :thumbsup: that wording works. Also recommend adding an explicit 'best-effort' note for model rollouts affecting quality.

mohit: Quick implementation note: sample router config for soft-priority we tested: ```yaml
route_priority: soft
weights:
  composer: 1.5
  standard: 1.0
burst_window_seconds: 600
max_burst_tokens: 200000
``` Put this in the RFC and it'll help rollout planning.

ana: Ok — I'll capture the RFC skeleton and ping the sales pilot owners. If we hit block on dedicated pools we can default to soft-priority for GA and reserve dedicated pools for Composer Pro.

legal: I'll flag indemnity and export-control clauses for pilot customers in regulated sectors.

ana: Final check — do we want a pricing pilot (discounted rate) or a free pilot? Sales wants discounted to capture commitment. Thoughts?

ralph: Discounted pilot with a small commit is better — avoids free usage and gives us billing telemetry. Maybe 25% off with a 3-month min commit.

sam: Agreed. Let's make pilot 25% off for up to 3 months with an option to convert to full commit. Add that to pilot addendum.

ana: Great. I'll update thread after the 3pm sync with notes + RFC link. Thanks everyone.

ops-bot: Export attached: https://internal.redwood/exports/top-routes-q4.csv (uploaded)

ana: (post-sync) notes added: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/commercial-composer-draft — includes SLOs, SKUs, implementation plan, and launch criteria. Next sync: T+3 days to review pilot contracts and eval results.
